label: Aristotle, Metaphysics XII.7, 1072b4-10: There is a mover that moves something, is moved in no…
interpretation: 'If something is moved, it can be otherwise; so if its actuality is primary locomotion, then in the respect in which it is moved it can be otherwise, in place, even if not in substance. But since there is something that moves while itself unmoved, being in act, this can in no way be otherwise (τοῦτο οὐκ ἐνδέχεται ἄλλως ἔχειν οὐδαμῶς); for locomotion is the first of changes, and circular locomotion the first of these, and this it causes.' Read as the sentence asserts it: existentially, of the mover whose existence 1072a21-26 has argued ('there is something which moves without being moved', ὃ οὐ κινούμενον κινεῖ). ἀκίνητον is read with that participle as 'not being moved' (not the modal 'cannot be moved'); ἐνεργείᾳ ὄν as being in act in the respect of being. οὐδαμῶς is read over the respects of change only (DEF-RESPECT-OF-CHANGE): the sentence contrasts the first heaven, otherwise in place but not in substance, and its reason is that the mover is not moved even by the first change; both 'unmoved' and 'in no way otherwise' are therefore read over the respects of change. Extending them to every respect, for a mover that moves something and is unmoved and unable to be otherwise in every respect of change, is the separate unattributed bridge STMT-UNCHANGEABLE-IN-RESPECTS-OF-CHANGE-IS-UNCHANGEABLE-SIMPLY. κινεῖ is read as the case's MovesIn; the mover moves as an object of love (1072b3), and reading MovesIn to include moving as an end is a reading choice recorded in DISAMB-MOTION. The reading does not say that every unmoved mover cannot be otherwise (sibling -B), that the mover is unique, or that it is pure act; it does not use ἀΐδιον (1072a25, b29) or the necessity of 1072b10-13.
